newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. senator says Tung to stand up for Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator says Tung to stand up for Hong Kong.

text.p: Hong Kong chief executive designate Tung Chee-hwa appears determined to stand up for citizens of the British colony when it reverts to Chinese rule, a U.S. senator who met Tung said on Friday.

"I think we should give Tung Chee-hwa ... and their group an opportunity to prove to the world because the world will be looking to them to take a stand when it's apppropriate relative to some of the demands that are likely to come down from Beijing," Senator Frank Murkowski said in Tokyo.

"He gave me the assurance that if those issues were to come forward he would respond accordingly in the best interest of Hong Kong," said the Alaska Republican of his meeting with Tung earlier this week.

Tung, a 59-year-old shipping magnate, on Wednesday was picked by a committee of 400 prominent Hong Kong citizens chosen by China to become chief executive when the British colony reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 next year, ending more than 150 years of British rule.

Murkowski, chairman of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, spoke to reporters on the final leg of a tour of Hong Kong, Taiwan and Japan. In Hong Kong, he met with Governor Chris Patten and Chief Secretary Anson Chang in addition to Tung.
"The PRC's (People's Republic of China's) credibility is somewhat on the line to ensure that the transition can occur smoothly," he told a news conference at the U.S. embassy.

"On the other hand there is some uncertainty for the future: currency assimilation, the presence of PRC in Hong Kong and the role of human rights and democratisation and the pace of each," Murkowski said.
The U.S. Congress would "closely watch to make sure the PRC lives up to the commitments of law" in its handling of Hong Kong, he said.
